# projr compatibility and change log

The [behavior contract](behavior.qmd) owns current product decisions. This log
records comparison evidence, implementation differences and gaps. Update it in
every focused PR; do not infer runtime parity from similar source or green Rust CI.

Relationship labels are **same**, **different**, **new**, and **unverified**.
Each entry states whether that label concerns documented intent, static source,
or executed behavior. No comparative R runtime tests have been run for the entries
below. Local R/Docker workloads have not been run.

## Reference baselines

- R baseline: [SATVILab/projr at 3ac2959](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/tree/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d).
- Thesis baseline: [design at b110da5](https://github.com/SATVILab/Manuscript22RodoThesis/blob/b110da557b802341e425f57f4acaa0c2b4ab97cb/projr/3-design.qmd).
- Rust pre-migration baseline: [024589b](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/tree/024589bbb6d471c3b1430057f76f5b2149444fac).

New comparisons must pin source commits and relevant files, record the decision
and rationale, link executed tests, and distinguish approved, implemented and
unverified behavior. Changing a reference baseline does not silently change the
product contract.

## PR123: development-preview mutation gates

- **Relationship: unverified runtime parity; same documented intent.** The R
  [README](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/README.md)
  and thesis design describe development previews separately from publication.
  This is evidence of intent, not proof that every R development path is inert.
- **Decision/rationale:** keep CLI-managed release/version/archive changes out of
  previews so researchers can inspect development results without publishing.
- **Implemented:** [PR123](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/123), merged
  `5d145293e596c5797e9620bd3f00978fa6f99411`; Dev-gated VERSION writes, cleanup,
  document promotion, local export and ignore updates in
  [build.rs](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/blob/5d145293e596c5797e9620bd3f00978fa6f99411/src/build.rs),
  env.rs and yml.rs.
- **Executed evidence:** [three-platform Rust tests](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39479251265),
  including `test_preview_safety.rs`, and installer checks passed on reviewed
  head `5d3ac227f52b33fd0c32fddd479cb7296c4072a5`. A disposable installed-CLI
  Python fixture reproduced the previous version/output/ignore mutations.
- **Gaps:** cooperating Python scripts only; renderer YAML rewriting, automatic
  output isolation, repeated runs, same-project concurrency and full production
  lifecycle behavior were not established. Subprocesses are not a sandbox.

## PR124: product authority and renderer contract

- **Relationship: new explicit contract; renderer parity unverified.** R
  [path.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/path.R)
  dynamically discovers a root, while the thesis defines the project workflow.
- **Decision/rationale:** current approved behavior supersedes defects and stale
  architecture claims. Root/path defaults must agree across projr,
  `quarto::quarto_render()` and RStudio QMD Render. Quarto root equals proj root;
  nested Quarto projects are unsupported. Direct rendering does not imply release
  lifecycle parity; R Markdown Knit is a separate entrypoint.
- **Implemented:** [PR124](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/124), merged
  `635aa9efac0d7a28971236ab78c879b21be5ec31`, corrected AGENTS/README/flow guidance
  and added the behavior contract. This was documentation, not renderer code.
- **Executed evidence:** independent document review and
  [remote Rust CI](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39481010442)
  passed at `dbf8d5fd94a87bba32ffc95cd2ee3b47f1e04277`.
- **Gaps:** no direct R frontend, Quarto/RStudio GUI or fresh-render-session
  parity test was performed. No projr production code or thesis text was changed.

## PR125: captured root and explicit selection

- **Relationship: different root-resolution mechanism; new CLI selection.** R
  [path.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/path.R)
  calls root discovery from current context. The CLI now captures one absolute
  root and passes it to each managed child as `PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT`.
- **Decision/rationale:** explicit selection wins, and path queries must not
  change projects after cwd changes. This deliberately improves unstable root
  behavior rather than copying it.
- **Implemented:** [PR125](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/125), merged
  `f265eb46c91a300fe0aafad3119d998038946a0b`; project.rs, ignore.rs, main.rs and
  build.rs. Direct library builds configure each child command instead of
  mutating the caller's process-global root.
- **Executed evidence:** [three-platform tests](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39481104695)
  at `779b3010040eeb23f08434478e0812173eb2a723` cover explicit precedence, spaces,
  invalid roots, changed cwd and overlapping builds in two distinct roots.
- **Gaps:** marker discovery was not changed; R path helpers and direct render
  entrypoints do not yet consume this captured context. The tests do not promise
  general environment isolation or same-project concurrent builds.

## PR126: nonmutating queries and initializer failure preservation

- **Relationship: same static read-only configuration intent; runtime R parity
  unverified.** R [yml.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/yml.R)
  reads/merges configuration; this does not establish equivalence of every R
  public path helper or its cache routing.
- **Decision/rationale:** reading configuration or paths must not update ignore
  files. Mutating build/init operations request synchronization explicitly, and
  bad configuration must not replace custom ignores with default rules.
- **Implemented:** [PR126](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/126), merged
  `cd34c3208f1ed1c3c27571e7ce2828498a4aecdb`; yml.rs, build.rs, init.rs/main.rs.
- **Executed evidence:** [three-platform tests](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39482261938)
  at `cc132f1e1b288c7560ff6b6b06fcac369a475355` snapshot files/directories for CLI
  queries, exercise direct API reads and production ignore synchronization, and
  preserve custom ignores on malformed/read-failing config. Permission-denied
  coverage ran on Linux/macOS.
- **Gaps:** supported aliases, unknown-option handling and effective merged
  script/hook configuration remained unchanged and incomplete.

## PR127: operation failures and exit status

- **Relationship: new CLI transport contract; same failure-reporting intent.** R
  [build-engine.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/build-engine.R)
  uses R errors; that is not a process exit-code protocol for language wrappers.
- **Decision/rationale:** a printed error must not be returned as successful
  execution. Failed Git remote inspection must not proceed to GitHub creation.
- **Implemented:** [PR127](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/127), merged
  `8e955b32bc1f611d38a8931d489de2bdfc50d5c7`; main.rs routes operation failures to
  nonzero status and init.rs propagates previously swallowed external failures.
- **Executed evidence:** [three-platform tests](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39482993953)
  at `a741b5f9de63dcb96ca527607105e5547be1da7c` cover failing queries/version/init/
  ignores, missing executables, child failure and successful queries. Local fake
  Git/GitHub commands on Linux/macOS made no network requests.
- **Gaps:** structured error/capability protocols and clean/idempotent Git-init
  coverage remained open; failure status is not rollback or R-runtime parity.

## PR128: explicit noninteractive execution

- **Relationship: new CLI mode.** The R baseline's
  [build-engine.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/build-engine.R)
  calls dependency helpers; no equivalent explicit CLI flag/parity is claimed.
- **Decision/rationale:** machine invocations must not need the CLI's prompts or
  automatic package installation. Controlled child stdin must actually be closed.
- **Implemented:** [PR128](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/128), merged
  `f7ff7e92451a3174d6cb9c5fd60151621e66bd04` after independent review at
  `5dedee7da69cbe52837993e86bc4837c4c3342a1`; adds the flag, inherited mode,
  runner stdin closure and controlled R-probe stdin closure.
- **Executed evidence:** [three-platform tests](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39484182256)
  and installer checks passed at that head; fake-R EOF/no-install tests ran on
  Linux/macOS and Python runner-stdin coverage ran on all three platforms.
- **Gaps:** no actual R startup/renderer execution comparison; initialization
  retains existing requested-operation defaults and third-party code can ignore
  EOF. This does not establish general subprocess isolation.

## PR129: explicit empty selection and newly confirmed policies

- **Relationship: same absent-dev fallback; different explicit-empty guarantee.** R
  [yml-scripts.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/yml-scripts.R)
  falls back when dev scripts are absent. Empty-list behavior also passes through
  [validation](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/yml-check.R)
  and renderer selection, so a reliable R upload-only no-analysis contract has
  not been demonstrated.
- **Decision/rationale:** explicit `[]` selects no analysis, preserving hooks and
  production upload/export; absence still falls back. It must not discover or
  render unrequested files. Cleanup/promotion must preserve upload inputs.
- **Implementation status:** [PR129](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/129)
  removes the Dev-empty error and derives one analysis-selection guard for
  renderer setup/cleanup/promotion. `tests/test_empty_scripts.rs` checks hooks,
  existing output/docs bytes, actual production archive bytes and preview
  nonpublication.
- **Executed evidence:** [three-platform Rust tests](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39485258868)
  and [installer checks](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39485258718)
  passed at `f4b3739554dc548911019c450ca1e90a196d33d2`; independent review inspected
  those logs and cleared that code head. The documentation-only final head
  `999b730fd2cc23215e4a07a1231d7d6fa3543966` passed all nine checks in
  runs 39486028024/39486028097 and independent review. Merged as
  `5617a6daed1f4743a9b2609694a2f84ad4c902eb`; post-merge test, installer
  and site runs 39486858711/39486858532/39486858701 passed.
- **Gaps:** YAML null-as-absence and malformed-list validation were inspected in
  source, not newly exercised by this policy slice. No R runtime empty-list parity
  test or real renderer execution is claimed.
- **Confirmed but separate runtime gaps:** retain projr markers (including README/
  VERSION), accept legacy `_projr.yml` with a both-base-files error, and use local
  > profiles > base with earlier profiles first. The R precedence evidence is
  [yml.R](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/yml.R#L224).
  These approvals are recorded in the behavior contract; this change does not
  implement aliases, marker expansion or merged script/hook context.

## Ponytail source verification and completed-chunk review

The actual [.agents/skills/ponytail/SKILL.md](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/blob/be625b670b914c85b669257eefd60ae678662d33/.agents/skills/ponytail/SKILL.md)
is vendored unchanged from DietrichGebert/ponytail **v4.10.0**, upstream commit
`e3ba2aa6f1e6f0bc4d69eb09c9f0d0a93af56156`, as installed by PR121. Its pinned
upstream bytes and the existing projcli, projr, setupmjr and projects copies all
have SHA-256 `1316a2f3f95741d2300b116fe0c2d81ce4a9568656ed0a62643f54aaf09957f2`.
The established setupmjr vendoring contract matches; no duplicate or replacement
skill was installed.

The skill prescribes the full-mode simplicity ladder, tracing callers before
changing shared behavior, reusing existing code/stdlib/dependencies, and leaving
an appropriate runnable check. It supplies no separate executable review script.
Applying that guidance is a self-review, separate from independent review and CI.

Completed-chunk review of PR128 at `5dedee7da69cbe52837993e86bc4837c4c3342a1`:

- Traced the prompt helpers, main description prompt, dependency probes, install
  branch, script/hooks and project-render runners. Reused the existing EnvGuard,
  one shared mode predicate and standard-library null stdin; no dependency or
  custom execution framework was introduced.
- Finding/action: the R package probe also needed closed stdin before package
  detection. That path was corrected and covered by a live-input/fake-R EOF test.
  Rechecking all controlled status/output paths found no further necessary change.
- All three remote Rust suites and installers passed; this self-review remained
  separate from the independent exact-head review.

Completed-chunk review of PR129's empty-selection change:

- Reused the existing explicit-list resolver and pipeline; no new execution
  framework, configuration key or dependency was added.
- Traced preflight, version, cleanup, hooks, document promotion and publication.
  Finding: skipping script execution alone could still erase upload-only inputs
  or require unused renderers. Action: derive one shared analysis-selection guard
  and apply it before those stages; keep hooks/publication outside that guard.
- Retained data-preservation and failure handling. Added runnable integration
  checks for real archive bytes and absence-versus-empty semantics; those checks
  passed on all three remote platforms at the code head recorded above. No R
  runtime parity was inferred.

## Nearest recognized roots (current change)

- **Relationship: same static projr marker intent; deliberate extensions.**
  [projr path.R at 3ac2959](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/path.R#L277)
  combines VCS, VERSION, README, R-package, RStudio, renv and Quarto criteria.
  Exact structured-marker patterns were checked in
  [rprojroot root.R at 4d2f450](https://github.com/r-lib/rprojroot/blob/4d2f450c3f67b98a3599fe8531bdda1c4c928cc1/R/root.R).
- **Decision/rationale:** retain those markers with nearest-wins; remove Rust's
  VERSION-first/five-extra-ancestors heuristic. Add pyproject.toml and Julia
  Project.toml/JuliaProject.toml as requested language extensions. Proj config
  files also anchor a configured project without VERSION. Requirements/orphan
  manifests do not create roots. Explicit selection still wins.
- **Implementation/evidence status:** `root_from` now tests each ancestor once,
  never child projects. `tests/test_root_markers.rs` covers retained marker
  patterns, invalid structured markers, weak/nested markers, deep invocation,
  explicit override and a configured Python preview with shallow enumeration.
  At code head `a0d459c5b3a31437443832436535b70d34838553`, all nine checks
  passed in runs 39487247962/39487247928. Independent review compared the pinned
  marker sources and inspected all three platform logs, clearing that head.
  Symlink normalization was source-inspected, without a new dedicated test.
  Final evidence-only head `55e5606e7916f78de7dfb03a4bb43b0ae1a87987`
  passed all nine checks in runs 39487685152/39487685131 and independent review;
  merged as `41bd7000363f34b1e7e2d7e354971bfe9021e2b1`. No R-runtime parity is claimed.
- **Gaps:** required active config, explicit used-directory mappings, early
  unsupported-setting validation, legacy config-content aliases and full
  frontend/renderer parity are separate changes. A marker does not claim a Julia runner exists.
- **Ponytail full-mode review:** reused the public root_from entrypoint, existing
  regex dependency and standard filesystem APIs, replacing the old special-case
  traversal instead of adding a discovery framework. Traced explicit/inherited
  precedence and all root callers. Kept discovery read-only and shallow, with
  runnable positive/negative predicates and workflow coverage; no new dependency.

## Superseding configuration, failure and R-scope decisions

- **Relationship: different from prior convenience-default assumptions.** The
  initial Rust/projr-style defaults and historical no-config fixtures are no
  longer the target behavior. Builds require active root-level configuration and
  explicit used-directory mappings; init may write familiar defaults into that
  file, but runtime must not invent missing directories or unknown subpaths.
- **Decision status:** approved. The agreed `_proj.yml` / legacy `_projr.yml`
  names apply; explicitly activated profile files may provide configuration,
  while inactive profiles alone do not satisfy the requirement. Cwd discovery
  fallback does not waive build validation. Unknown behavior-affecting settings
  must fail before mutation.
- **Failure/publication target:** restore pre-build state except permitted cache
  residue; storage/publication retry must not rerun or mislabel analysis. Existing
  staging/version/publication behavior does not yet prove that transaction.
- **Evidence/gaps:** earlier CI entries remain accurate historical evidence for
  their source commits, not acceptance of the superseded no-config/default-path
  policy. Future fixtures must declare used paths and active configuration.
  The current core still needs enforcement and failure tests for the new rules.
- **Authorship boundary:** the existing R package is entirely off limits, including
  root-helper fixes. A later backend port/integration must establish R parity;
  no such work or runtime comparison is claimed here. Thesis text remains untouched.


## Base aliases and profile precedence (current change)

- **Relationship:** same projr local > profiles > base precedence, with
  earlier-listed profiles winning; legacy `_projr.yml` is accepted alongside
  canonical `_proj.yml` as an explicit compatibility decision. Both base files
  together fail instead of silently merging. Source comparison remains
  [projr yml.R at 3ac2959](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/blob/3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d/R/yml.R#L224).
- **Implemented:** shared base selection for merged reads, existing build base
  inspection, parameters insertion and local-profile cloning. Explicit profile
  lists replace ambient lists; traversal-like explicit names fail validation.
  Profile/local files retain their existing `_projr-` names in this bounded slice.
- **Evidence:** new runnable query/alias/ambiguity/preservation/precedence tests
  passed on all three platforms at `53463d325c85c538ae0b8a5e792caa6bc997e452`.
  All nine checks in runs 39488461110/39488461213 passed; independent review
  inspected alias, precedence and duplicate-key logs and cleared that head.
  Final documentation/instruction head `c8b208f9243f828de05977f8e76d6f2074535a9b`
  passed all nine checks in runs 39489639669/39489639654 and independent review;
  merged as `0fec2735355ee5e9b9ba64d33ecd4796bf396301`. Post-merge checks passed.
  No R runtime tests.
- **Gaps:** one merged build script/hook context, active-configuration requirement,
  explicit directory mappings and early unsupported-setting validation remain
  separate work. This does not claim builds yet satisfy those approved rules.
- **Ponytail full-mode review:** traced base filename readers and reused one
  stdlib path selector; reversed existing deep-merge traversal rather than adding
  a merger or dependency. Preserved null-as-absence and explicit-empty-list
  behavior. Checks exercise real query results and preservation on ambiguity.


PR131 failure-path review found that direct YAML-to-JSON deserialization allowed
duplicate keys to overwrite earlier values. Restored YAML Value parsing before
JSON conversion, preserving duplicate-key rejection at every active layer.
Added top-level and nested duplicate-key regressions for both base filenames,
profile and local files, including CLI failure before preview state writes.
The prior green CI did not cover this malformed-input case; the corrected head
above passed the new checks and independent re-review. Ponytail review kept this at the
shared file parser rather than guarding individual callers.

## Future R wrapper distribution boundary

- **Relationship: new/unverified design.** The
  [durable CRAN note](r-wrapper-cran.qmd) records the discussed future R-code wrapper
  around a separately installed CLI, meaningful unconditional R-only/mocked tests,
  conditional executable integration on CRAN, and mandatory pinned/checksummed CLI
  integration in our own CI. It cites current policy and pinned Quarto precedent.
- No existing R code or tests were changed; no CRAN submission, agreement,
  preinstalled executable, automatic-download exemption or renderer parity is
  claimed. Implementation and runtime validation remain future work.
- **Ponytail full-mode design review:** kept one linked design note; reused the

## One merged build script/hook context (current change)

- **Relationship:** follows projr's merged-configuration intent and the approved
  local > earlier profiles > later profiles > base precedence. The prior Rust
  pipeline validated merged settings but separately reread the base for execution.
- **Implemented:** deserialize and validate one merged value, then select scripts
  and hooks from it. Explicit empty dev selection remains empty; absence falls
  back to build settings. Both base filenames use this same execution path.
  Configuration parsing/validation, target resolution and preflight now precede
  production environment-ignore writes.
- **Evidence:** runnable Python fixtures check conflicting profiles, legacy base,
  local dev overrides and hook results, plus invalid merged configuration with a
  local environment file and missing-target failures leaving ignores/version/cache untouched. Remote CI and
  independent review pending; no real R/renderer execution is claimed.
- **Gaps:** required active config, explicit mappings, all unsupported-field
  rejection and transactional rollback remain separate approved work. Environment
  loading still uses the existing process-global guard; this change makes no new
  same-process concurrent environment guarantee.
- **Ponytail full-mode review:** removed the second base-only YAML parser and its
  ignored parse failure instead of adding a second configuration model. Reused
  existing typed validation and dev fallback rules. Traced validation, selection,
  hooks and environment-ignore writes; retained explicit error propagation.


## Legacy audit tracking

The [2026-10-20 static audit](legacy-audit-20261020.qmd) records the pinned baseline,
reported failure paths, required regressions and correction order. Its findings
are not runtime reproductions or completed fixes. Highest managed-state risks
remain blockers to production-safety claims; arbitrary external script effects
are outside managed rollback. No mechanical edition upgrade or CAS redesign is
claimed. This review uses the actual Ponytail full-mode skill to prioritize root
causes and data-preservation checks over cosmetic rewriting.

## Active configuration and unsupported fields (prepared change)

- **Relationship: deliberate difference** from projr convenience defaults, as
  explicitly approved. Every build requires a base file or activated profile;
  inactive profile/local files alone do not qualify. Discovery still falls back
  to cwd independently. Empty analysis is valid with active configuration.
- **Implemented:** build gate before writes; unsupported typed configuration
  fields fail instead of disappearing in a top-level filter. Build failures
  include their error causes so unsupported-field diagnostics name the field. Arbitrary parameter
  and metadata maps remain supported and parameter aliases reach validation.
- **Evidence:** runnable tests cover active/base/legacy/inactive/local/no-config
  cases, unsupported nested keys, dynamic maps and no pre-build state writes.
  Remote CI/independent review pending. Explicit directory enforcement is still
  a separate gap; this does not yet establish transaction/promotion safety.
- **Ponytail full-mode review:** reused Serde's unknown-field validation and the
  existing active profile resolver; removed silent filtering from runtime reads.
  No new parser/schema/dependency. Kept the old public filter helper only for
  compatibility; runtime no longer uses it.

PR135 review found mixed parameter aliases survived per-file parsing as separate
keys and then conflicted at typed deserialization. Canonicalize the one accepted
alias to `parameters` in the shared reader before merging. New fixtures cover all
64 base/profile/local alias combinations, earlier-profile precedence and retained
nested values; same-file multiple aliases and YAML duplicate keys remain errors.
Ponytail full-mode re-review kept the fix at the shared loader, without caller
guards or a second merge model. Exact amended CI/re-review remain required.

## Destructive destination guards (prepared change)

- **Relationship: new safety checks**, not a blanket ban on external resources.
  Before production analysis cleanup, reject root/ancestor destinations, staging
  and resource overlaps, selected-input containment, VCS metadata, label path
  separators and symlinked managed-write paths. Directory replacement also
  requires an existing source and disjoint destination before deleting bytes.
- **Evidence:** runnable preservation fixtures cover root, ancestor, staging,
  raw/output overlaps, traversal labels, Unix symlink parents and low-level
  self/ancestor/nested/missing-source moves. Remote CI/review pending.
- **Limits:** does not yet provide atomic promotion or complete rollback, protect
  against concurrent hostile filesystem replacement, undo user-script external
  effects or establish full CAS integrity. External disjoint paths remain valid.
- **Ponytail full-mode review:** one stdlib identity resolver shared by build and
  promotion guards; trace all promotion callers, retain explicit errors instead
  of silently accepting missing source/read errors. No new dependency.


Path-guard Ponytail re-review traced the public cleanup helpers as well as build:
direct clear_pre/clear_post now apply the shared destination checks, clear_old
rejects symlinked staging parents, and traversal-bearing version components fail
before cache deletion. Label separator validation lives in shared typed validation
for all modes. Generic destructive move APIs require resolved parents and reject
symlink aliases; positive direct-API fixtures canonicalize their temporary roots
so macOS system temp aliases do not violate that explicit safety precondition.
Added a direct-cleanup preservation fixture. This is not complete transactional
restoration or a guarantee against concurrent filesystem replacement.
